messages:
maria: heads-up — noticed 2 accounts still in `admin` group after last SCIM run, but okta shows them deactivated. possible permission drift.
jonathan: can you paste the usernames?
maria: svc-analytics, tony.h (internal user). scim audit shows group-sync job completed at 2026-03-03T14:02Z.
scim-bot: group-sync completed org=redwood job=gs-20260303-1402 status=success processed=128 added=0 removed=2
maria: weird — removed=2 but these two still show active in our RBAC store.
jonathan: ok. likely a mismatch between SCIM delete and our local role binding cleanup.
lee: running quick query to confirm:```sql
SELECT external_id, scim_status, local_rbac, last_sync
FROM scim_provisioning
WHERE external_id IN ('svc-analytics','tony.h');
```
lee: results: svc-analytics scim_status=deactivated local_rbac=[admin] last_sync=2026-03-03T14:02Z; tony.h scim_status=deactivated local_rbac=[admin] last_sync=2026-03-03T14:02Z
anika: so our sync job marks them removed but the role cleanup step must have errored or skipped. any error logs?
lee: checking logs now — found this in group-sync-worker:```text
ERROR: cleanupBindings: permission-check failed for user 'svc-analytics' reason="missing-lookup-key"
Trace: KeyNotFoundError at path /secrets/scim/user_lookup_key
```
maria: missing-lookup-key = config bug. that's likely from recent KMS rotation patch we shipped last week.
tamir: ouch. KMS rotation took effect but the worker didn't pick up the new key id. we saw a small window where secrets read would fail.
jonathan: can we force cleanup now? we should revoke admin privileges urgently.
lee: I can run the revoke script against the local RBAC store:```bash
./tools/rbac-revoke --users svc-analytics tony.h --dry-run
```
lee: dry-run OK, will run live in 2m unless objections.
maria: go for it, but add audit reason and link to this thread.
lee: running:```bash
./tools/rbac-revoke --users svc-analytics tony.h --reason "SCIM deprovision sync failure - cleanup"
```
lee: done. both users removed from admin group. confirmed via query.
jonathan: nice. can we patch group-sync to fail hard when KMS read fails and add retry + alert?
anika: +1. current behavior is to log error and continue which causes orphaned bindings. we should make cleanup an idempotent separate job with dead-lettering.
tamir: I'll open an infra ticket to add a guard: if secrets fetch fails, pause cleanup and create incident. also add a metric admin_orphan_count that alerts on >0 for >5m.
tamir: ticket: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/4521
lee: also opened PR to handle missing-lookup-key gracefully and to requeue cleanup: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/9876 (unit tests + integration test simulating KMS rotation).
maria: please include steps to backfill — for any user with scim_status=deactivated and local admin, schedule revoke and attach audit reason. we should run over last 7 days.
jonathan: query to find all orphans:```sql
SELECT external_id FROM scim_provisioning WHERE scim_status='deactivated' AND ARRAY_CONTAINS(local_rbac,'admin') AND last_sync > now() - interval '7 days';
```
lee: running that now, will produce list and run revokes in batch with exponential backoff.
sre-bot: incident created INC-2026-041: SCIM cleanup failed during KMS rotation, orphaned admin accounts detected. paging oncall.
maria: pinging customer success for any customer-facing impact — likely internal only but we should be thorough.
anika: quick note: KMS key rotation plan updated to include rollout to group-sync workers and a small health-check to verify secret fetch post-rotation. I'll add to runbook.
tamir: reminder: add an audit log entry for the revokes with operator id and reason.
lee: done — audit events written to audit-log-service with refs.
maria: thanks. follow-ups: 1) monitor admin_orphan_count alert 2) merge PR 9876 3) run 7-day backfill 4) post mortem in #postmortems if we see related incidents.
jonathan: I'll own the postmortem if needed.
maria: great. closing loop once backfill completes. :thumbsup:
